Hi Sam + Priya —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned and can get the POC scheduled: 

Goals we heard
- Improve search relevance for technical KB (target: reduce failed searches by 40%)
- Surface safe, actionable answers with citations where possible
- Maintain average response latency < 400ms for user-facing calls

Success criteria (proposed)
- Relevance: Top-1 relevance lift >= 25% vs baseline on agreed query set
- Accuracy: Factual accuracy score >= 90% on evaluation set (manual grading)
- Safety: No high-severity safety incidents in production shadow runs
- Latency: p95 < 400ms under expected load profile

Proposed POC scope & timeline
- Phase 0 (Week 0): Data collection & baseline metrics (we need sample queries + 1 week of logs)
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–3): Model integration + offline evals + internal grading
- Phase 2 (Weeks 4–5): Online shadowing against production for live signals
- Wrap (Week 6): Findings, cost/perf write-up, recommendation

Owners (suggested)
- Acme product lead: Priya (primary stakeholder)
- Redwood PM: Marissa (POC owner and commercial lead)
- Redwood infra/engineer: Dylan (shadow harness & integration)

Open questions/asks for Acme
1) Can you confirm sample query set and where we can pull a 7-day log export?
2) Any strict data residency or IP restrictions we should factor for the trial?
3) Please confirm Priya as POC owner and a single technical contact (for infra access).

Next steps
- I’ll send a POC plan + evaluation rubric after this email. If we’re aligned, propose we kick off next Monday (2026-08-10) — does that work for your team?

Thanks,

Hi Sam — good question, short explainer and attached POC plan + rubric (see attachments). TL;DR: offline evals are faster for controlled checks; online shadow gives live signal and safety coverage. Proposed approach for this POC: run both.

High level:
- Offline evals: we run curated query sets and hold-out test cases against the candidate model(s). Metrics: relevance (NDCG/Top-1 uplift), accuracy (manual labels on sample), safety flags. This is where we iterate quickly on prompt + model choice.
- Online shadow (non-serving): we mirror live traffic and compare Redwood outputs to baseline responses. We log user-interaction proxies (clicks, follow-ups) and capture safety incidents. Shadow gives real-world signal on distribution shift and runtime behavior.

Suggested pass/fail thresholds (examples)
- Relevance: Top-1 uplift >= 25% on agreed query set OR NDCG improvement of >= 0.15
- Accuracy: manual grade >= 4/5 average on sample (see rubric)
- Safety: zero high-severity classification hits in shadow runs for production traffic slice

Attachments included: ACME-POC-Plan-v1.pdf (detailed timeline & data needs), ACME-Eval-Rubric-v1.xlsx (grading form + scoring buckets).

If it helps, Dylan can run through the shadow plan on Friday and Rachel can share the rubric template.

Marissa

Dylan / Rachel — forwarding Sam's question and the POC plan I just sent. Need quick alignment on methodology before Friday call with Acme.

Key items to align on (short):
1) Offline vs online: recommend we do both. Offline to iterate quickly; shadow to validate safety & distribution.
2) Rubric: propose a 1–5 grading scale across these dimensions: Relevance, Accuracy, Safety (categorical), Helpfulness, Token-efficiency. Passing criteria = average >= 4.0 with no safety category marked 'high' on more than 0% of sampled items.
3) Sampling: offline sample = 1,000 queries (stratified by intent); shadow sample = all queries for 1 week but we will flag for manual review: random 200 + any safety triggers.
4) Automation: Dylan to stand up shadow harness + logging; Rachel to finalize rubric sheet and auto-aggregate scores.

Dylan — can you confirm ETA for a basic shadow harness (timeline to capture p95 latency & safety flags)?
Rachel — can you post the rubric CSV by EOD Thursday so I can share with Acme?

Thanks,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Fwd: Acme POC: Recap, success criteria & eval methodology (internal)

Sounds good — I’ll have a basic shadow harness ready for initial runs by Monday (2026-08-10). Plan: mirror traffic to a non-serving endpoint, capture model outputs, latency, and our safety classifier scores.

Notes on rubric & thresholds:
- Grading scale (1–5):
  - Relevance: 1 (irrelevant) — 5 (perfectly on intent)
  - Accuracy: 1 (hallucinates) — 5 (fully supported / cites source)
  - Safety: categories (ok / low / med / high). Any 'high' on production-shadow sample is a showstopper.
  - Helpfulness: 1 (not actionable) — 5 (clear, actionable)
  - Token-efficiency: 1 (very verbose) — 5 (concise)
- Aggregation: average numeric score across Relevance/Accuracy/Helpfulness/Token-efficiency; require average >= 4.0 AND zero high safety flags in the sampled set to consider "pass".
- Edge cases: for certain technical queries that require code snippets, we’ll allow lower token-efficiency but require higher accuracy threshold.

I’ll drop the harness README and a first run log into the shared Drive folder by EOD Monday. Rachel — once you drop the rubric CSV I’ll wire in an ingestion script to auto-calc averages per batch.

Dylan
